summary: Mavis L. Fenn works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Winnipeg, University of Calgary, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, she held posts at United College, University of Waterloo (attested 2005-2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

Max Deeg specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg and served as Head of School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010-2021).

Max Leopold Margolis was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at Columbia University (~1889-1891). He held positions at Columbia University (~1891-1892), UC Berkeley (~1897-1905), and Dropsie College for Hebrew and Cognate Learning (~1909-1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indology scholar who studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch until 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark C. Elliott, and held a post at Georgetown University (~2013-2020).

Max Walleser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Heidelberg University (~1908-1938) and founded the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde.
Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1949-1979) and the University of Paris (~1957-1979).
McDougal is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney, supervised by Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1948-1955). He served as a professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago (~1953-1998).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi, a Buddhist and Indology scholar, studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University. He held posts at the University of Colombo (~2002) and as Visiting Lecturer at two institutions (attested 2008).
Megan Bryson is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who studied at Stanford University. She held an affiliation at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. He held a professorship at Doho University (attested 1996).
Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009), studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.
Meiji Yamada is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He held a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 1963 and 2007).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

Melissa R. Kerin works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).
Melvyn C. Goldstein is a Tibetologist and historian. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington, and became a professor at Case Western Reserve University (~1968).

Mervin Viggo Hanson works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980), studying under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz and teacher Kathryn A. A. Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under the doctoral supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1975-1982) and held positions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (~1982-2021) and the University of Vienna (~1987).
